skills.name: anchoring
skills.description: First information disproportionately influences judgments and decisions, even when the initial value is arbitrary or irrelevant

skills.name: availability-heuristic
skills.description: Correct probability and frequency judgments distorted by mentally available examples by seeking base rate data before relying on vivid anecdotes

skills.name: confirmation-bias
skills.description: Combat the tendency to seek evidence supporting existing beliefs by actively searching for disconfirming data and treating opinions as testable hypotheses

skills.name: dunning-kruger-effect
skills.description: Low-skill individuals overestimate their competence because they lack the metacognitive ability to recognize their own incompetence

skills.name: fundamental-attribution-error
skills.description: Over-attributing others' behavior to their character while under-weighting situational factors that shape their actions

skills.name: halo-effect
skills.description: One positive trait creates a global positive impression, influencing judgments about unrelated characteristics

skills.name: hindsight-bias
skills.description: The tendency to perceive past events as more predictable than they actually were, leading to distorted learning and overconfidence

skills.name: sunk-cost-fallacy
skills.description: Continuing an endeavor due to previously invested resources (time, money, effort) rather than current and future costs and benefits, escalating commitment to failing courses of action

skills.name: thinking-circle-of-competence
skills.description: Know the boundaries of your expertise and operate within them. Use when evaluating opportunities, making decisions outside your domain, or assessing when to defer to experts.

skills.name: thinking-debiasing
skills.description: Systematic checklist to identify and counteract cognitive biases in decision-making. Use before major decisions, when evaluating recommendations, or when stakes are high.

skills.name: thinking-dual-process
skills.description: Apply Kahneman's Dual-Process Theory to recognize when to trust intuition vs engage deliberate analysis. Use for high-stakes decisions, error-prone contexts, or when balancing speed vs accuracy.

skills.name: thinking-map-territory
skills.description: Recognize limits of mental models and diagrams. Use when models diverge from reality, debugging expectation mismatches, or questioning abstraction accuracy.

skills.name: eisenhower-matrix
skills.description: Prioritize tasks by urgency and importance—focus on important but not urgent work to prevent firefighting

skills.name: rice-prioritization
skills.description: Scoring framework using Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort to objectively prioritize product features and projects

skills.name: schelling-fence
skills.description: Strategic precommitment to defend an arbitrary line on a slippery slope. Use when you face a continuum from acceptable to unacceptable and need a conspicuous, defensible boundary.

skills.name: thinking-bounded-rationality
skills.description: Apply Herbert Simon's Bounded Rationality and satisficing to make good-enough decisions under real-world constraints. Use for design decisions under time pressure, recognizing cognitive limits, and setting appropriate stopping criteria.

skills.name: thinking-cynefin
skills.description: Classify problems by complexity domain (clear, complicated, complex, chaotic) and match approach to domain. Use for choosing methodologies, problem framing, and process design.

skills.name: thinking-inversion
skills.description: Approach problems backward by identifying paths to failure, then systematically avoiding them. Use for risk identification, planning, and avoiding obvious mistakes.

skills.name: thinking-lindy-effect
skills.description: For non-perishable things, future life expectancy is proportional to current age. Use for technology selection, evaluating frameworks/libraries, and predicting tool longevity.

skills.name: thinking-margin-of-safety
skills.description: Build in buffers for unknown unknowns and don't optimize to the edge. Use for capacity planning, deadline estimation, architecture design, and risk management.

skills.name: thinking-ooda
skills.description: Rapid decision-making loop for dynamic situations. Use for incident response, competitive scenarios, time-sensitive decisions, and situations requiring quick adaptation.

skills.name: thinking-pre-mortem
skills.description: Imagine a project has failed and work backward to identify why. Use at project kickoffs, before major decisions, or when optimism may be obscuring risks.

skills.name: thinking-red-team
skills.description: Deliberately attack your own plans, systems, and assumptions to find weaknesses before adversaries or reality does. Use for security review, architecture validation, plan stress-testing, and pre-launch preparation.

skills.name: thinking-regret-minimization
skills.description: Project to your future self and ask what you would regret not doing. Use for career decisions, strategic pivots, risk-taking choices, and life-changing decisions.

skills.name: thinking-reversibility
skills.description: Classify decisions by reversibility and match decision process to decision type. Use for technology choices, architecture decisions, process changes, and hiring decisions.

skills.name: thinking-via-negativa
skills.description: Improve by removal rather than addition. Focus on what to stop doing, eliminate the negative, and subtract complexity. Use for system simplification, process improvement, and feature prioritization.

skills.name: current-reality-tree
skills.description: A logical diagram that maps cause-effect relationships between undesirable effects to identify root causes that drive most organizational problems

skills.name: fault-tree-analysis
skills.description: Top-down deductive methodology for analyzing system failures by mapping logical relationships between faults, subsystems, and redundant safety elements using Boolean logic diagrams

skills.name: fishbone-diagram
skills.description: Visually map all potential causes of a problem across structured categories to systematically identify root causes through team collaboration

skills.name: thinking-five-whys-plus
skills.description: Enhanced root cause analysis with explicit bias guards and stopping criteria. Use for incident post-mortems, bug investigations, and process failures where standard 5 Whys might mislead.

skills.name: thinking-kepner-tregoe
skills.description: Systematic rational process for complex problem analysis, decision making, and risk assessment. Use for high-stakes engineering decisions, root cause analysis beyond 5 Whys, and multi-factor evaluations requiring structured criteria.

skills.name: calibration
skills.description: Align predicted probabilities with actual outcomes - train yourself so things you say are 70% likely actually happen 70% of the time

skills.name: monte-carlo-simulation
skills.description: Probabilistic modeling technique that runs thousands of scenarios with random variable inputs to quantify uncertainty and assess risk distributions

skills.name: outside-view-inside-view
skills.description: Forecast by comparing to similar past cases (outside view) instead of analyzing unique project details (inside view) - cures planning fallacy

skills.name: sensitivity-analysis
skills.description: Systematic testing of how changes in input variables (assumptions) affect output results, revealing which factors drive outcomes and where model risk is concentrated.

skills.name: superforecasting
skills.description: Make probabilistic predictions when strategic decisions require accurate risk assessment

skills.name: tetlocks-10-commandments
skills.description: Improve forecast accuracy by following Philip Tetlock's 10 evidence-based principles from superforecaster research distinguishing top 2% predictors

skills.name: thinking-bayesian
skills.description: Update beliefs systematically based on new evidence using probabilistic reasoning. Use when estimating probabilities, learning from data, or making decisions under uncertainty.

skills.name: thinking-fermi-estimation
skills.description: Make order-of-magnitude estimates for unknown quantities by decomposing into known or estimable factors. Use for capacity planning, cost estimation, market sizing, and technical feasibility assessment.

skills.name: thinking-in-bets
skills.description: Frame decisions as probability bets instead of certainties - separate decision quality from outcome quality to avoid resulting bias

skills.name: thinking-probabilistic
skills.description: Express confidence in ranges, update predictions with new information, and track calibration over time. Use for project estimation, risk assessment, and decision making under uncertainty.

skills.name: wisdom-of-crowds-aggregation
skills.description: Combine diverse independent estimates to produce more accurate predictions than any single expert, when conditions support collective intelligence

skills.name: compound-interest
skills.description: Leverage exponential growth by reinvesting gains to earn returns on returns, whether in finance, skills, relationships, or habits—small consistent improvements compound into transformational outcomes

skills.name: goodharts-law
skills.description: Anticipate metric gaming and unintended optimization by recognizing that when a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure

skills.name: incentives
skills.description: Predict and shape behavior by understanding the hidden rewards and punishments that drive human action

skills.name: mechanism-design
skills.description: Reverse game theory that engineers rules and incentive structures to achieve desired outcomes when participants have private information and self-interested motivations

skills.name: nash-equilibrium
skills.description: Identify stable strategic outcomes where no player benefits from unilaterally changing their strategy - predict where competitive dynamics settle

skills.name: principal-agent-problem
skills.description: Conflicts arising when one party (agent) makes decisions on behalf of another (principal), but their interests diverge and information is asymmetric

skills.name: prisoners-dilemma
skills.description: Recognize situations where individual rational choices lead to collectively worse outcomes - core model for cooperation vs. defection dynamics

skills.name: thinking-opportunity-cost
skills.description: Evaluate decisions by what you give up, not just what you gain. Use for resource allocation, prioritization, build vs. buy choices, and technical debt evaluation.

skills.name: thinking-second-order
skills.description: Think beyond immediate consequences to second and third-order effects. Use for strategic decisions, policy changes, and avoiding unintended consequences.

skills.name: time-value-of-money
skills.description: Value money received today higher than the same amount in the future because present money can be invested to earn returns—use Net Present Value to compare cash flows across time and make rational investment decisions

skills.name: tit-for-tat
skills.description: Start new business relationships with trust and investment, but immediately match any breach. Return to cooperation as soon as they do. Make the pattern obvious through transparency.

skills.name: chestertons-fence
skills.description: Before removing something, understand why it was put there in the first place—reforms without understanding cause unintended consequences

skills.name: hanlons-razor
skills.description: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by incompetence

skills.name: hitchens-razor
skills.description: What can be asserted without evidence can be dismissed without evidence

skills.name: humes-guillotine
skills.description: You cannot derive an 'ought' from an 'is' without bridging logic

skills.name: poppers-falsifiability
skills.description: Scientific theories must be testable and capable of being proven false

skills.name: sagan-standard
skills.description: Calibrate evidence requirements proportional to claim implausibility when evaluating extraordinary assertions

skills.name: thinking-first-principles
skills.description: Break complex problems into fundamental truths by questioning assumptions and rebuilding from irreducible components. Use for innovation, challenging status quo, or when conventional solutions fail.

skills.name: thinking-occams-razor
skills.description: Apply parsimony principle to prefer simpler explanations with fewer assumptions. Use for hypothesis selection in debugging, architecture decisions, and choosing between competing approaches.

skills.name: thinking-scientific-method
skills.description: Hypothesis → Prediction → Test → Revise with explicit falsification. Use for debugging, feature experimentation, performance investigation, and A/B testing design.

skills.name: thinking-socratic
skills.description: Systematic questioning framework to deepen understanding, challenge assumptions, and uncover hidden beliefs. Use for requirements gathering, debugging, coaching, and critical analysis.

skills.name: thinking-steel-manning
skills.description: Argue against the strongest version of opposing positions, not the weakest. Use for design reviews, evaluating alternatives, conflict resolution, and decision validation.

skills.name: thinking-thought-experiment
skills.description: Test ideas through hypothetical scenarios when empirical testing is impractical. Use for architecture evaluation, edge case analysis, ethics considerations, and strategy development.

skills.name: good-strategy-bad-strategy
skills.description: Craft coherent strategy through diagnosis of core challenge, guiding policy, and coordinated actions when facing complex problems requiring more than goals and aspirations

skills.name: pest-analysis
skills.description: Generate PEST analysis plans with strategic questions and Perplexity AI prompts. Use when user mentions PEST analysis, strategic planning, market analysis, external factors, environmental scanning, or needs research questions for political economic social technological factors.

skills.name: pest-analysis-critical
skills.description: Critically evaluate PEST synthesis tables for biases, gaps, and oversights. Use when user mentions critical review, bias assessment, gap analysis, or after completing PEST synthesis.

skills.name: pest-analysis-execute
skills.description: Execute PEST analysis by processing research results from Perplexity AI prompts. Create synthesis tables with strategic implications, impact and likelihood ratings. Use when user mentions PEST results, analysis execution, research synthesis, or after generating PEST analysis plans.

skills.name: pest-analysis-strategy
skills.description: Transform PEST analysis into actionable strategy: export to CSV, save to Obsidian, create SWOT, define strategic actions, prioritize, and build work plan. Use after completing PEST critical assessment.

skills.name: pest-analysis-synthesis
skills.description: Create PEST synthesis tables with strategic implications, impact and likelihood ratings. Use when user mentions synthesis table, strategic recommendations, opportunity threat analysis, or after completing PEST research.

skills.name: playing-to-win
skills.description: Five-question strategy cascade framework for making integrated strategic choices from winning aspiration to management systems, from P&G's transformation

skills.name: porters-five-forces
skills.description: Systematically assess the competitive intensity and attractiveness of an industry by analyzing five fundamental forces that shape competition and profitability

skills.name: thinking-effectuation
skills.description: Start with means, not goals; co-create with partners; leverage contingencies. Use for startup strategy, innovation projects, and uncertain/novel domains where planning is unreliable.

skills.name: thinking-jobs-to-be-done
skills.description: Understand what 'job' users hire your product to do, focusing on progress users seek rather than features. Use for product development, feature prioritization, user research, and market positioning.

skills.name: thinking-triz
skills.description: Apply TRIZ (Theory of Inventive Problem Solving) methodology to resolve technical contradictions and find innovative solutions. Use for engineering design, breaking through impossible constraints, and systematic innovation.

skills.name: three-horizons-framework
skills.description: Balance current business performance with emerging opportunities and future innovation by allocating resources across three time horizons of growth

skills.name: causal-loop-diagrams
skills.description: Map cause-and-effect relationships with reinforcing/balancing feedback loops to visualize system structure and predict behavior patterns

skills.name: graph-thinking
skills.description: Apply graph-based thinking to visualize complex relationships and solve problems non-linearly. Use when mapping dependencies, analyzing systems, exploring interconnected concepts, or designing architectures.

skills.name: thinking-archetypes
skills.description: Recognize Senge's Systems Archetypes to diagnose recurring organizational and technical problems, identify why fixes keep failing, and design interventions that address root structure.

skills.name: thinking-feedback-loops
skills.description: Analyze systems using Donella Meadows' feedback loop framework to identify reinforcing loops, balancing loops, delays, and leverage points. Use for organizational dynamics, product growth design, debugging runaway or oscillating systems, and finding high-impact interventions.

skills.name: thinking-leverage-points
skills.description: Identify where small changes can have large effects using Donella Meadows' hierarchy of system intervention points. Use for strategic decisions, system optimization, and choosing where to focus engineering effort.

skills.name: thinking-systems
skills.description: Analyze problems as interconnected systems with feedback loops, emergent behavior, and non-linear effects. Use for debugging complex systems, architecture decisions, and understanding unexpected behavior.

skills.name: thinking-theory-of-constraints
skills.description: Identify and manage the bottleneck; improvements elsewhere don't matter until the constraint is addressed. Use for performance optimization, process improvement, and resource allocation.
